startup_quarantine.text: Quarantine new plants for about 2 weeks: inspect leaves and roots, treat if needed. Do not plant straight into the shared jar — this keeps pests and mold out.

startup_stone_test.text: Stones {stone_names} may raise pH: drop vinegar on them. Fizzing means carbonates — keep them away from mosses and carnivores.

startup_stone_soak.text: Soak stones {stone_names} for {days} days, changing the water, to remove dust and soluble salts.

startup_substrate_prep.text: Prepare the substrate components ({components}): rinse sand and clay pebbles, boil or bake bark, rinse charcoal dust, hydrate coco.

startup_cleanup_crew.text: Establish springtails {lead_time_weeks} weeks before planting: they will eat mold and litter and prime the ecosystem.

startup_layers.text: Build the layers in order: {layer_order}. Do not skip drainage and charcoal — without them the substrate turns sour.

startup_calibration.text: For the first 2 weeks calibrate moisture by condensation: if dry, add {dose_ml} ml and recheck after {recheck_hours} h. Under-water rather than over-water.

light_placement.text: Your spot: {placement_label}. Species were matched to this light. Do not place the jar in direct rays — glass amplifies overheating.

light_lamp.text: {species} needs supplemental light: a grow light {photoperiod_h} h/day at {distance_cm} cm distance.

light_no_direct_sun.text: Do not put a sealed jar in direct sun: the glass acts as a greenhouse, internal temperature rises 10–15 °C and cooks the plants. Bright indirect light is required.

light_winter_boost.text: Winter light is weaker — increase supplemental light by {boost_h} h/day, especially for light-loving species.

water_closed.text: In a sealed jar moisture cycles around, so watering is almost unnecessary. Water only if the substrate turns dry, and very little. Follow condensation, not a schedule.

water_open_tropical.text: Check the substrate: when the top 1–2 cm dries, water at the roots, not on leaves. Roughly every {interval_weeks} weeks.

water_open_succulent.text: Water succulents sparingly: let the substrate dry out completely, then water. Roughly every {interval_weeks} weeks, less in winter.

water_carnivore_open.text: Carnivores in an open system: keep a {tray_cm} cm water tray constantly. Distilled, RO or rain water only.

water_carnivore_closed.text: Carnivores in a closed system: keep the substrate constantly moist but without standing water at root level. Distilled or RO only.

vent_closed.text: Air the sealed jar: {schedule}. This prevents stagnant air and mold.

vent_mold.text: Mold is kept in check by springtails and ventilation, not charcoal. Remove fallen leaves — they are a mold source.

season_cool_winter.text: {species} needs a cool winter rest: months {months}, temperature {temp_c} °C. Reduce watering in winter.

season_dry_winter.text: {species} needs a dry winter rest: months {months}, temperature {temp_c} °C. Barely water in winter.

season_summer.text: In summer shade the jar from direct sun and ventilate against overheating. Use sheer fabric on a south window.

prune_aggressive.text: Aggressive species ({species}) will smother neighbours — trim regularly and do not let them take over the jar.

fauna_feeding.text: {name}: feed every {interval_days} days ({items}). Remove leftovers so they do not mold.

fauna_calcium_local.text: Place calcium (cuttlebone) locally on a feeding station, not in acid substrate — otherwise you raise pH and harm acid-loving plants.

fauna_litter.text: Leaf litter in the decor is already food for the cleanup crew. Refresh it every {refresh_weeks} weeks.

fauna_nematodes.text: Apply nematodes per the manufacturer's instructions (millions of individuals per pack). Keep the substrate moist; repeat after 2–3 weeks against gnat larvae.

water_distilled.text: Water {species} with distilled, RO or rain water only. Hard water is lethal.

water_soft.text: {species} is sensitive to hard water — use soft filtered water, otherwise limescale on glass and brown leaf tips.

limescale.text: White dry crust on the glass is hard-water salts, not mold. Wipe it off and switch to soft water.

monocarpic.text: {species} blooms once: the rosette dies after flowering. Keep the offsets — they will carry on the plant.

day_night_drop.text: {species} needs a 5–8 °C day/night drop, otherwise pitchers will not form. It struggles in a warm flat without a drop.

epiphyte_mount.text: {species} is an epiphyte: mount it on driftwood or cork bark, do not plant in substrate. Mist or soak.

tillandsia.text: Tillandsia is atmospheric: no substrate needed, mount it. Soak 20–30 min every 1–2 weeks or mist 2–3 times a week. After soaking, shake water out of the rosette centre.

bromeliad_cup.text: For bromeliads ({species}) pour water into the rosette cup, but make sure it does not stagnate and rot — flush the cup periodically.

bom_layers.text: Shopping list from your vessel's floor: drainage {drainage_l} L, substrate {substrate_name} {substrate_l} L, charcoal {charcoal_ml} ml.

bom_lamp.text: Grow light: PPFD {ppfd_range} µmol/m²/s, photoperiod {photoperiod_h} h/day.
